Dark Souls III.name: Dark Souls III

progression_balancing.description:
A system that can move progression earlier, to try and prevent the player from getting stuck and bored early.

A lower setting means more getting stuck. A higher setting means less getting stuck.

accessibility.description:
Set rules for reachability of your items/locations.

**Full:** ensure everything can be reached and acquired.

**Minimal:** ensure what is needed to reach your goal can be acquired.

local_items.description: Forces these items to be in their native world.

non_local_items.description: Forces these items to be outside their native world.

start_inventory.description: Start with the specified amount of these items. Example: "Bomb: 1"

start_hints.description: Start with these item's locations prefilled into the ``!hint`` command.

start_location_hints.description: Start with these locations and their item prefilled into the ``!hint`` command.

exclude_locations.description: Prevent these locations from having an important item.

priority_locations.description: Prevent these locations from having an unimportant item.

item_links.description: Share part of your item pool with other players.

early_banner.description: Force Small Lothric Banner into an early sphere in your world or across all worlds.

late_basin_of_vows.description:
Guarantee that you don't need to enter Lothric Castle until later in the run.

- **Off:** You may have to enter Lothric Castle and the areas beyond it immediately after High
  Wall of Lothric.
- **After Small Lothric Banner:** You may have to enter Lothric Castle after Catacombs of
  Carthus.
- **After Small Doll:** You won't have to enter Lothric Castle until after Irithyll of the
  Boreal Valley.

late_dlc.description:
Guarantee that you don't need to enter the DLC until later in the run.

- **Off:** You may have to enter the DLC after Catacombs of Carthus.
- **After Small Doll:** You may have to enter the DLC after Irithyll of the Boreal Valley.
- **After Basin:** You won't have to enter the DLC until after Lothric Castle.

death_link.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

enable_dlc.description:
Include DLC locations, items, and enemies in the randomized pools.

To use this option, you must own both the "Ashes of Ariandel" and the "Ringed City" DLCs.

enable_ngp.description: Include items and locations exclusive to NG+ cycles.

random_starting_loadout.description: Randomizes the equipment characters begin with.

require_one_handed_starting_weapons.description: Require starting equipment to be usable one-handed.

auto_equip.description: Automatically equips any received armor or left/right weapons.

lock_equip.description:
Lock the equipment slots so you cannot change your armor or your left/right weapons.

Works great with the Auto-equip option.

no_equip_load.description: Disable the equip load constraint from the game.

no_weapon_requirements.description:
Disable the weapon requirements by removing any movement or damage penalties, permitting you
to use any weapon early.

no_spell_requirements.description: Disable the spell requirements permitting you to use any spell.

randomize_infusion.description: Enable this option to infuse a percentage of the pool of weapons and shields.

randomize_infusion_percentage.description: The percentage of weapons/shields in the pool to be infused if Randomize Infusion is toggled.

randomize_weapon_level.description:
Enable this option to upgrade a percentage of the pool of weapons to a random value between
the minimum and maximum levels defined.

- **All:** All weapons are eligible, both basic and epic
- **Basic:** Only weapons that can be upgraded to +10
- **Epic:** Only weapons that can be upgraded to +5

randomize_weapon_level_percentage.description: The percentage of weapons in the pool to be upgraded if randomize weapons level is toggled.

min_levels_in_5.description: The minimum upgraded value of a weapon in the pool of weapons that can only reach +5.

max_levels_in_5.description: The maximum upgraded value of a weapon in the pool of weapons that can only reach +5.

min_levels_in_10.description: The minimum upgraded value of a weapon in the pool of weapons that can reach +10.

max_levels_in_10.description: The maximum upgraded value of a weapon in the pool of weapons that can reach +10.

smooth_soul_items.description:
Distribute soul items in a similar order as the base game.

By default, soul items will be distributed totally randomly. If this is set, less valuable soul
items will generally appear in earlier spheres and more valuable ones will generally appear
later.

smooth_upgrade_items.description:
Distribute upgrade items in a similar order as the base game.

By default, upgrade items will be distributed totally randomly. If this is set, lower-level
upgrade items will generally appear in earlier spheres and higher-level ones will generally
appear later.

smooth_upgraded_weapons.description:
Distribute upgraded weapons in a similar order as the base game.

By default, upgraded weapons will be distributed totally randomly. If this is set, lower-level
weapons will generally appear in earlier spheres and higher-level ones will generally appear
later.

simple_early_bosses.description:
Avoid replacing Iudex Gundyr and Vordt with difficult bosses.

This limits these fights to bosses that are known to scale gracefully for low-level fights.
This doesn't necessarily mean that those bosses will be from the early game, just that they're
not too difficult when scaled down.

This is ignored unless enemies are randomized.

scale_enemies.description:
Scale randomized enemy stats to match the areas in which they appear.

Disabling this will tend to make the early game much more difficult and the late game much
easier.

This is ignored unless enemies are randomized.

randomize_mimics_with_enemies.description:
Mix Mimics into the main enemy pool.

If this is enabled, Mimics will be replaced by normal enemies who drop the Mimic rewards on
death, and Mimics will be placed randomly in place of normal enemies. It's recommended to enable
Impatient Mimics as well if you enable this.

This is ignored unless enemies are randomized.

randomize_small_crystal_lizards_with_ene.displayName: Randomize Small Crystal Lizards With Enemies
randomize_small_crystal_lizards_with_ene.description:
Mix small Crystal Lizards into the main enemy pool.

If this is enabled, Crystal Lizards will be replaced by normal enemies who drop the Crystal
Lizard rewards on death, and Crystal Lizards will be placed randomly in place of normal enemies.

This is ignored unless enemies are randomized.

reduce_harmless_enemies.description:
Reduce the frequency that "harmless" enemies appear.

Enable this to add a bit of extra challenge. This severely limits the number of enemies that are
slow to aggro, slow to attack, and do very little damage that appear in the enemy pool.

This is ignored unless enemies are randomized.

all_chests_are_mimics.description:
Replace all chests with mimics that drop the same items.

If "Randomize Mimics With Enemies" is set, these chests will instead be replaced with random
enemies that drop the same items.

This is ignored unless enemies are randomized.

impatient_mimics.description:
Mimics attack as soon as you get close instead of waiting for you to open them.

This is ignored unless enemies are randomized.

random_enemy_preset.description:
The YAML preset for the static enemy randomizer.

See the static randomizer documentation in `randomizer\presets\README.txt` for details.
Include this as nested YAML. For example:

.. code-block:: YAML

  random_enemy_preset:
    RemoveSource: Ancient Wyvern; Darkeater Midir
    DontRandomize: Iudex Gundyr

excluded_location_behavior.description:
How to choose items for excluded locations in DS3.

- **Allow Useful:** Excluded locations can't have progression items, but they can have useful
  items.
- **Forbid Useful:** Neither progression items nor useful items can be placed in excluded
  locations.
- **Do Not Randomize:** Excluded locations always contain the same item as in vanilla Dark Souls
  III.

A "progression item" is anything that's required to unlock another location in some game. A
"useful item" is something each game defines individually, usually items that are quite
desirable but not strictly necessary.

missable_location_behavior.description:
Which items can be placed in locations that can be permanently missed.

- **Allow Useful:** Missable locations can't have progression items, but they can have useful
  items.
- **Forbid Useful:** Neither progression items nor useful items can be placed in missable
  locations.
- **Do Not Randomize:** Missable locations always contain the same item as in vanilla Dark Souls
  III.

A "progression item" is anything that's required to unlock another location in some game. A
"useful item" is something each game defines individually, usually items that are quite
desirable but not strictly necessary.

EarthBound.name: EarthBound

progression_balancing.description:
A system that can move progression earlier, to try and prevent the player from getting stuck and bored early.

A lower setting means more getting stuck. A higher setting means less getting stuck.

accessibility.description:
Set rules for reachability of your items/locations.

**Full:** ensure everything can be reached and acquired.

**Minimal:** ensure what is needed to reach your goal can be acquired.

local_items.description: Forces these items to be in their native world.

non_local_items.description: Forces these items to be outside their native world.

start_inventory.description: Start with the specified amount of these items. Example: "Bomb: 1"

start_hints.description: Start with these item's locations prefilled into the ``!hint`` command.

start_location_hints.description: Start with these locations and their item prefilled into the ``!hint`` command.

exclude_locations.description: Prevent these locations from having an important item.

priority_locations.description: Prevent these locations from having an unimportant item.

item_links.description: Share part of your item pool with other players.

giygas_required.description:
If enabled, your goal will be to defeat Giygas at the Cave of the Past.
If disabled, your goal will either complete automatically upon completing
enough Sanctuaries, or completing Magicant if it is required.

sanctuaries_required.description: How many of the eight "Your Sanctuary" locations are required to be cleared.

skip_prayer_sequences.description: If enabled, the Prayer cutscenes while fighting Giygas will be skipped, excluding the final one.

random_start_location.description:
If disabled, you will always start at Ness's house with no teleports unlocked.
If enabled, you will start at a random teleport destination with one teleport unlocked.
Additionally, you will need to fight Captain Strong to access the north part of Onett if this is enabled.

alternate_sanctuary_goal.description:
If enabled, you will be able to win by completing 2 more Sanctuaries than are required.
Does nothing if 7 or more Sanctuaries are required, or if Magicant and Giygas are not required.

magicant_mode.description:
PSI Location: You will be able to find a Magicant teleport item. Ness's Nightmare contains a PSI location, and no stat boost.
Required: You will unlock the Magicant Teleport upon reaching your Sanctuary goal. If Giygas is required, beating Ness's Nightmare will unlock the Cave of the Past and grant a party-wide stat boost. Otherwise, Ness's Nightmare will finish your game.
Alternate Goal: You will unlock the Magicant Teleport upon reaching one more Sanctuary than required. Beating Ness's Nightmare will finish your game. Does nothing if Giygas is not required, or if 8 Sanctuaries are required. Magicant locations are removed from the multiworld, but contain random junk for yourself.
Optional Boost: You will be able to find a Magicant teleport item. Beating Ness's Nightmare will grant a party-wide stat boost. Magicant locations are removed from the multiworld, but contain random junk for yourself.
Removed: Magicant will be completely inacessible.

monkey_caves_mode.description:
Chests: Items required to finish the Monkey Caves will be forcibly placed on the chests that can be found in-between rooms of the monkey caves. The "reward" locations, usually found at the end of a branch, are still random. If you waste chest items, they will need to be replaced via the methods in hunt mode.
Hunt: Items required to finish the Monkey Caves will needsell you every minor item needed to be found outside. They can be obtained from the Dusty Dunes drugstore, the Fourside department store, and the pizza shop in either Twoson or Threed.
Shop: The monkey outside the Monkey Caves will sell every item needed to complete the caves and is not affected by shop randomization.
Solved: The Monkey Caves monkeys will already be moved out of the way and not require any items.

local_teleports.description: Forces all teleports and Poo PSI to be placed locally in your world.

character_shuffle.description:
Shuffled: Characters will be shuffled amongst Character Locations. Extra locations will have Flying Man, a Teddy Bear, or a Super Plush Bear.
Anywhere: Characters can be found anywhere in the multiworld, and character locations will have regular checks.
See the Game Page for more information on Character Locations.

starting_character.description:
Sets which character you start as. Each character will always start with the ability to teleport,
and the ATM card. Ness will not be required to fight Sanctuary bosses.

psi_shuffle.description:
None: Characters will learn their normal PSI skills.
Basic: Offensive and Assist PSI will be shuffled. Recovery PSI is not modified. Ness's Favorite Thing will be named Wave in other slots.
Extended: Basic shuffle, but includes Jeff gadgets and some combat items.
See the Game Page for more information.

allow_flash_as_favorite_thing.description:
If enabled, allows PSI Flash to be shuffled onto the Favorite Thing PSI slot. Can be quite annoying early-game. 
Does nothing if PSI Shuffle is set to None.

enemy_shuffle.description: Shuffles Non-boss enemies amongst each other.

boss_shuffle.description: Shuffles boss encounters amongst each other.

decouple_diamond_dog.description:
Shuffles Diamond Dog as a boss separate from Carbon Dog. Carbon Dog will transform into a random boss.
Does nothing if Boss Shuffle is disabled.

boss_shuffle_add_giygas.description:
Adds the standalone Giygas fight to the shuffled boss pool.
This only applies to the second phase Giygas. The prayer fight is not affected.
Does nothing if Boss Shuffle is disabled.

safe_final_boss.description:
Prevents specific difficult bosses from being randomized onto Heavily Armed Pokey's boss slot.
Only affects Boss Shuffle, and does not affect Phase 2 Giygas if Boss Shuffle Add Giygas is enabled.

randomize_enemy_attributes.description: Randomizes most attributes of non-boss enemies.

randomize_enemy_stats.description: Randomizes base stats and level of non-boss enemies.

experience_modifier.description: Percentage of EXP enemies give you. 100 is vanilla, after scaling, and 300 is x3.

money_drop_multiplier.description: Multiplies money dropped by enemies by the chosen value.

starting_money.description: How much money you start with.

easy_deaths.description: Fully revives and heals all party members after death. If off, only Ness will be healed with 0 PP.

easy_combat.description: Automatically halves all scaled enemy levels.

progressive_weapons.description: If enabled, Bats, Fry Pans, and Guns will be progressive. Does not apply to items dropped by enemies or found in shops.

progressive_armor.description: If enabled, Bracelets and items for the Other slot besides Ribbons will be progressive. Does not apply to items dropped by enemies or found in shops.

armorizer.description:
All equippable armor will have randomly generated attributes. This includes who can equip it, elemental resistance (and how strong that resistance is),
defense, and the secondary stat it increases (Either Luck or Speed, depending on armor slot.) Choosing "Help!" from the Goods menu will give you exact details
on that piece of equipment.
Keep Type: Equipment will keep its original equipment slot. If Progressive Armor is enabled, you will get armor with progressively higher defense. 
Chaos: Equipment will have a randomly selected slot. It will try to respect the defense progressively, but the type may not match the type received.

weaponizer.description:
All weapons will have randomly generated attributes. This includes offense, guts boost, and miss rate.
Keep Type: Equipment will keep the character that was originally able to use it. If Progressive Weapons is enabled, you will get weapons with progressively higher offense.
Chaos: Equipment will be able to be equipped by a randomly selected character. It will try to respect the offense progresively, but the type may not match the type recieved.
The Tee Ball Bat will always be a weapon for Ness.

armorizer_resistance_chance.description:
Percent chance for any given Body/Other equipment to have elemental protection.
Affects Armorizer only.

equipamizer_cap_stats.description:
If enabled, the highest value that Equipamizer can roll for a piece of equipment's
main stat will be capped. 80 for armor, 125 for weapons.
If disabled, the main stat can potentially roll up to 128.

auto_scale_party_members.description: If enabled, joining party members will be scaled to roughly the level of the sphere they were obtained in.

remote_items.description:
If enabled, you will receive your own items from the server upon collecting them, rather than locally.
This allows co-op within the same game, and protects against loss of save data.
However, you will not be able to play offline if this is enabled.

random_flavors.description: Randomizes the non-plain window color options.

random_swirl_colors.description: Generates random colors for pre-battle swirls.

presents_match_contents.description: If enabled, Presents, Trash cans, and chests will have their appearance modified to be indicative of the item they contain.

nonlocal_items_use_local_presents.description:
If enabled, present that contain items for other players will appear as EarthBound presents (trashcan, present, and chest) instead of Archipelago boxes.
Does nothing if Presents Match Contents is disabled.

prefixed_items.description:
If enabled, broken items in the multiworld pool will be replaced with their fixed versions.
This does not affect any items that are not placed by the multiworld.

total_photos.description: How many Photograph traps are placed in the item pool.

randomize_franklinbadge_protection.description:
If enabled, the Franklin Badge will reflect a randomly selected attack type. The type can be determined from the item's name, as well as the help
text for it. The badge's function outside of battle will not change, and neither will its name outside of the game itself.

shuffle_enemy_drops.description:
If enabled, enemies will drop random filler items. This does not put checks on enemy drops.
Drop rates are unchanged.

common_filler_weight.description: Weight for placing a common filler item.

uncommon_filler_weight.description: Weight for placing an uncommon filler item.

rare_filler_weight.description: Weight for placing a rare filler item.

money_weight.description: Weight for placing money in the item pool.

plando_lumine_hall_text.description: Set text to be displayed at Lumine Hall. If nothing is entered, random community-submitted text will be selected instead.

no_free_sanctuaries.description:
If enabled, the entrance to Lilliput Steps and Fire Spring will be locked and require extra key items to access.
These items are the Tiny Key and Tenda Lavapants, respectively.

randomize_overworld_music.description:
Randomizes music on the overworld. Some sound effects might sound weird.
Normal: Does not randomize music.
Match Type: Music will be randomized with similar song categories (Town, dungeon, etc.)
Full: Overworld music will be randomized disregarding categories.

randomize_psi_palettes.description:
Randomizes the colors of PSI spells.
Normal: Doesn't randomize PSI colors.
Shuffled: PSI spell palettes are swapped around with each other.
Randomized: PSI spells use completely random colors.

map_palette_shuffle.description:
Randomizes map colors.
Normal: Uses normal colors
Nice: Uses generally good looking palettes for maps with little artifacting.
Ugly: Allows map palettes with artifacting or colors that may not look good.
Nonsense: Allows really bad palettes or heavy artifacting.

shop_randomizer.description:
Randomizes items in shops.
Local Filler: Shops contain only random items for yourself and are not checks.
Shopsanity. Every shop slot in the game contains a Multiworld location. ONLY ENABLE SHOPSANITY IF YOU KNOW WHAT YOU ARE DOING.

scout_shop_checks.description: Scouts Shop checks when you open a shop. Only affects shops in Shopsanity mode.

dungeon_shuffle.description: Shuffles Dungeon entrances amongst each other.

skip_epilogue.description:
If enabled, the choice to play the epilogue after beating Giygas will be removed, and you will
go directly to the credits. This option is mainly for no-release seeds where checks could be
potentially spoiled in the open-access epilogue.

start_inventory_from_pool.description:
Start with the specified amount of these items and don't place them in the world. Example: "Bomb: 1"

The game decides what the replacement items will be.

death_link.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

death_link_mode.description:
Controls how receiving a Deathlink functions in battle.
Instant: The player will be instantly defeated.
Mortal: All characters will receieve mortal damage. The player will not be able to heal until the battle is finished.
Mortal Mercy: All characters will receieve mortal damage, but the player will be able to heal it before they die.
Regardless of this setting, receiving a deathlink outside of battle will always instantly defeat the player.

energy_link.description:
If enabled, the money in the ATM will be linked across the Archipelago Server.
This requires a server connection to be used, but won't break offline play.

local_items.description: Forces these items to be in their native world.

non_local_items.description: Forces these items to be outside their native world.

start_inventory.description: Start with the specified amount of these items. Example: "Bomb: 1"

start_hints.description: Start with these item's locations prefilled into the ``!hint`` command.

start_location_hints.description: Start with these locations and their item prefilled into the ``!hint`` command.

exclude_locations.description: Prevent these locations from having an important item.

priority_locations.description: Prevent these locations from having an unimportant item.

item_links.description: Share part of your item pool with other players.

max_science_pack.description:
Maximum level of science pack required to complete the game.
This also affects the relative cost of silo and satellite recipes if they are randomized.
That is the only thing in which the Utility Science Pack and Space Science Pack settings differ.

goal.description: Goal required to complete the game.

craftsanity.description:
Choose a number of researches to require crafting a specific item rather than with science packs.
May be capped based on the total number of locations.
There will always be at least 2 Science Pack research locations for automation and logistics, and 1 for rocket-silo
if the Rocket Silo option is not set to Spawn.

tech_tree_layout.description:
Selects how the tech tree nodes are interwoven.
Single: No dependencies
Diamonds: Several grid graphs (4/9/16 nodes each)
Pyramids: Several top halves of diamonds (6/10/15 nodes each)
Funnels: Several bottom halves of diamonds (6/10/15 nodes each)
Trees: Several trees
Choices: A single balanced binary tree

min_tech_cost.description: The cheapest a Technology can be in Science Packs.

max_tech_cost.description: The most expensive a Technology can be in Science Packs.

tech_cost_distribution.description:
Random distribution of costs of the Science Packs.
Even: any number between min and max is equally likely.
Low: low costs, near the minimum, are more likely.
Middle: medium costs, near the average, are more likely.
High: high costs, near the maximum, are more likely.

tech_cost_mix.description:
Percent chance that a preceding Science Pack is also required.
Chance is rolled per preceding pack.

ramping_tech_costs.description:
Forces the amount of Science Packs required to ramp up with the highest involved Pack. Average is preserved.
For example:
off: Automation (red)/Logistics (green) sciences can range from 1 to 1000 Science Packs,
on: Automation (red) ranges to ~500 packs and Logistics (green) from ~500 to 1000 Science Packs

silo.description: Ingredients to craft rocket silo or auto-place if set to spawn.

free_samples.description: Get free items with your technologies.

free_samples_quality.description:
If free samples are on, determine the quality of the granted items.
Requires the quality mod, which is part of the Space Age DLC. Without it, normal quality is given.

tech_tree_information.description:
How much information should be displayed in the tech tree.
None: No indication of what a research unlocks.
Advancement: Indicates if a research unlocks an item that is considered logical advancement, but not who it is for.
Full: Labels with exact names and recipients of unlocked items; all researches are prefilled into the !hint command.

starting_items.description: Mapping of Factorio internal item-name to amount granted on start.

free_sample_blacklist.description: Set of items that should never be granted from Free Samples

free_sample_whitelist.description: Overrides any free sample blacklist present. This may ruin the balance of the mod, be warned.

recipe_time.description:
Randomize the time it takes for any recipe to craft, this includes smelting, chemical lab, hand crafting etc.
Fast: 0.25X - 1X
Normal: 0.5X - 2X
Slow: 1X - 4X
Chaos: 0.25X - 4X
New category: ignores vanilla recipe time and rolls new one
New Fast: 0.25 - 2 seconds
New Normal: 0.25 - 10 seconds
New Slow:  5 - 10 seconds

recipe_ingredients.description: Select if rocket, or rocket + science pack ingredients should be random.

recipe_ingredients_offset.description:
When randomizing ingredients, remove or add this many "slots" of items.
For example, at -1 a randomized Automation Science Pack will only require 1 ingredient, instead of 2.

imported_blueprints.description: Allow or Disallow Blueprints from outside the current savegame.

world_gen.description:
World Generation settings. Overview of options at https://wiki.factorio.com/Map_generator,
with in-depth documentation at https://lua-api.factorio.com/latest/concepts/MapGenSettings.html

progressive.description:
Merges together Technologies like "automation-1" to "automation-3" into 3 copies of "Progressive Automation",
which awards them in order.

teleport_traps.description:
Trap items that when received trigger a random teleport.
It is ensured the player can walk back to where they got teleported from.

grenade_traps.description: Trap items that when received trigger a grenade explosion on each player.

cluster_grenade_traps.description: Trap items that when received trigger a cluster grenade explosion on each player.

artillery_traps.description: Trap items that when received trigger an artillery shell on each player.

atomic_rocket_traps.description:
Trap items that when received trigger an atomic rocket explosion on each player.
Warning: there is no warning. The launch is instantaneous.

atomic_cliff_remover_traps.description:
Trap items that when received trigger an atomic rocket explosion on a random cliff.
Warning: there is no warning. The launch is instantaneous.

inventory_spill_traps.description: Trap items that when received trigger dropping your main inventory and trash inventory onto the ground.

attack_traps.description: Trap items that when received trigger an attack on your base.

evolution_traps.description: Trap items that when received increase the enemy evolution.

evolution_trap_increase.description:
How much an Evolution Trap increases the enemy evolution.
Increases scale down proportionally to the session's current evolution factor
(40 increase at 0.50 will add 0.20... 40 increase at 0.75 will add 0.10...)

death_link.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

energy_link.description: Allow sending energy to other worlds. 25% of the energy is lost in the transfer.

start_inventory_from_pool.description:
Start with the specified amount of these items and don't place them in the world. Example: "Bomb: 1"

The game decides what the replacement items will be.

Prevents the Shop's Red Potions from being shuffled. Those locations
will have purchasable Red Potion as usual for their usual price.

include_pendant.description:
Pendant is an item that boosts your attack power permanently when picked up.
However, due to a programming error in the original game, it has the reverse
effect. You start with the Pendant power, and lose it when picking
it up. So this item is essentially a trap.
There is a setting in the client to reverse the effect back to its original intend.
This could be used in conjunction with this option to increase or lower difficulty.

include_poisons.description:
Whether or not to include Poison Potions in the pool of items. Including them
effectively turn them into traps in multiplayer.

require_dragon_slayer.description:
Requires the Dragon Slayer to be available before fighting the final boss is required.
Turning this on will turn Progressive Shields into progression items.

This setting does not force you to use Dragon Slayer to kill the final boss.
Instead, it ensures that you will have the Dragon Slayer and be able to equip
it before you are expected to beat the final boss.

random_musics.description:
All levels' music is shuffled. Except the title screen because it's finite.
This is an aesthetic option and doesn't affect gameplay.

random_sounds.description:
All sounds are shuffled.
This is an aesthetic option and doesn't affect gameplay.

random_npcs.description:
NPCs and their portraits are shuffled.
This is an aesthetic option and doesn't affect gameplay.

random_monsters.description:
Choose how monsters are randomized.
"Vanilla": No randomization
"Level Shuffle": Monsters are shuffled within a level
"Level Random": Monsters are picked randomly, balanced based on the ratio of the current level
"World Shuffle": Monsters are shuffled across the entire world
"World Random": Monsters are picked randomly, balanced based on the ratio of the entire world
"Chaotic": Completely random, except big vs small ratio is kept. Big are mini-bosses.

progression_balancing.description:
A system that can move progression earlier, to try and prevent the player from getting stuck and bored early.

A lower setting means more getting stuck. A higher setting means less getting stuck.

accessibility.description:
Set rules for reachability of your items/locations.

**Full:** ensure everything can be reached and acquired.

**Minimal:** ensure what is needed to reach your goal can be acquired.

**Items:** ensure all logically relevant items can be acquired. Some items, such as keys, may be self-locking, and
some locations may be inaccessible.

local_items.description: Forces these items to be in their native world.

non_local_items.description: Forces these items to be outside their native world.

start_inventory.description: Start with the specified amount of these items. Example: "Bomb: 1"

start_hints.description: Start with these item's locations prefilled into the ``!hint`` command.

start_location_hints.description: Start with these locations and their item prefilled into the ``!hint`` command.

exclude_locations.description: Prevent these locations from having an important item.

priority_locations.description: Prevent these locations from having an unimportant item.

item_links.description: Share part of your item pool with other players.

logic.description:
Placement logic sets the rules that will be applied when placing items. Friendly: Required Items to clear a
dungeon will never be placed in that dungeon to avoid the need to revisit it. Also, the Magic Mirror and the Mask
will always be available before Ice Pyramid and Volcano, respectively. Note: If Dungeons are shuffled, Friendly
logic will only ensure the availability of the Mirror and the Mask. Standard: Items are randomly placed and logic
merely verifies that they're all accessible. As for Region access, only the Coins are considered. Expert: Same as
Standard, but Items Placement logic also includes other routes than Coins: the Crests Teleporters, the
Fireburg-Aquaria Lava bridge and the Sealed Temple Exit trick.

brown_boxes.description:
Include the 201 brown box locations from the original game. Brown Boxes are all the boxes that contained a
consumable in the original game. If shuffle is chosen, the consumables contained will be shuffled but the brown
boxes will not be Archipelago location checks.

sky_coin_mode.description:
Configure how the Sky Coin is acquired. With standard, the Sky Coin will be placed randomly. With Start With, the
Sky Coin will be in your inventory at the start of the game. With Save The Crystals, the Sky Coin will be acquired
once you save all 4 crystals. With Shattered Sky Coin, the Sky Coin is split in 40 fragments; you can enter Doom
Castle once the required amount is found. Shattered Sky Coin will force brown box locations to be included.

shattered_sky_coin_quantity.description:
Configure the number of the 40 Sky Coin Fragments required to enter the Doom Castle. Only has an effect if
Sky Coin Mode is set to shattered. Low: 16. Mid: 24. High: 32. Random Narrow: random between 16 and 32.
Random Wide: random between 10 and 38.

progressive_gear.description: Pieces of gear are always acquired from weakest to strongest in a set.

starting_companion.description:
Set a companion to start with.
Random Companion: Randomly select one companion.
Random Plus None: Randomly select a companion, with the possibility of none selected.

available_companions.description:
Select randomly which companions will join your party. Unavailable companions can still be reached to get their items and complete their quests if needed.
Note: If a Starting Companion is selected, it will always be available, regardless of this setting.

companions_locations.description:
Set the primary location of companions. Their secondary location is always the same.
Standard: Companions will be at the same locations as in the original game.
Shuffled: Companions' locations are shuffled amongst themselves.
Shuffled Extended: Add all the Temples, as well as Phoebe's House and the Rope Bridge as possible locations.

kaelis_mom_fight_minotaur.description:
Transfer Kaeli's requirements (Tree Wither, Elixir) and the two items she's giving to her mom.
Kaeli will be available to join the party right away without the Tree Wither.

companion_leveling_type.description:
Set how companions gain levels.
Quests: Complete each companion's individual quest for them to promote to their second version.
Quests Extended: Each companion has four exclusive quests, leveling each time a quest is completed.
Save the Crystals (All): Each time a Crystal is saved, all companions gain levels.
Save the Crystals (Individual): Each companion will level to their second version when a specific Crystal is saved.
Benjamin Level: Companions' level tracks Benjamin's.

companion_spellbook_type.description:
Update companions' spellbook.
Standard: Original game spellbooks.
Extended: Add some extra spells. Tristam gains Exit and Quake and Reuben gets Blizzard.
Random Balanced: Randomize the spellbooks with an appropriate mix of spells.
Random Chaos: Randomize the spellbooks in total free-for-all.

enemies_density.description: Set how many of the original enemies are on each map.

enemies_scaling_lower.description: Randomly adjust enemies stats by the selected range percentage. Include mini-bosses' weaker clones.

enemies_scaling_upper.description: Randomly adjust enemies stats by the selected range percentage. Include mini-bosses' weaker clones.

bosses_scaling_lower.description:
Randomly adjust bosses stats by the selected range percentage. Include Mini-Bosses, Bosses, Bosses' refights and
the Dark King.

bosses_scaling_upper.description:
Randomly adjust bosses stats by the selected range percentage. Include Mini-Bosses, Bosses, Bosses' refights and
the Dark King.

enemizer_attacks.description:
Shuffles enemy attacks. Standard: No shuffle. Safe: Randomize every attack but leave out self-destruct and Dark
King attacks. Chaos: Randomize and include self-destruct and Dark King attacks. Self Destruct: Every enemy
self-destructs. Simple Shuffle: Instead of randomizing, shuffle one monster's attacks to another. Dark King is left
vanilla.

enemizer_groups.description: Set which enemy groups will be affected by Enemizer.

shuffle_res_weak_types.description: Resistance and Weakness types are shuffled for all enemies.

shuffle_enemies_position.description: Instead of their original position in a given map, enemies are randomly placed.

progressive_formations.description:
Enemies' formations are selected by regions, with the weakest formations always selected in Foresta and the
strongest in Windia. Disabled: Standard formations are used. Regions Strict: Formations will come exclusively
from the current region, whatever the map is. Regions Keep Type: Formations will keep the original formation type
and match with the nearest power level.

doom_castle_mode.description:
Configure how you reach the Dark King. With Standard, you need to defeat all four bosses and their floors to
reach the Dark King. With Boss Rush, only the bosses are blocking your way in the corridor to the Dark King's room.
With Dark King Only, the way to the Dark King is free of any obstacle.

doom_castle_shortcut.description:
Create a shortcut granting access from the start to Doom Castle at Focus Tower's entrance.
Also modify the Desert floor, so it can be navigated without the Mega Grenades and the Dragon Claw.

tweak_frustrating_dungeons.description:
Make some small changes to a few of the most annoying dungeons. Ice Pyramid: Add 3 shortcuts on the 1st floor.
Giant Tree: Add shortcuts on the 1st and 4th floors and curtail mushrooms population.
Pazuzu's Tower: Staircases are devoid of enemies (regardless of Enemies Density settings).

map_shuffle.description:
None: No shuffle. Overworld: Only shuffle the Overworld locations. Dungeons: Only shuffle the dungeons' floors
amongst themselves. Temples and Towns aren't included. Overworld And Dungeons: Shuffle the Overworld and dungeons
at the same time. Everything: Shuffle the Overworld, dungeons, temples and towns all amongst each others.
When dungeons are shuffled, defeating Pazuzu won't teleport you to the 7th floor, you have to get there normally to
save the Crystal and get Pazuzu's Chest.

crest_shuffle.description: Shuffle the Crest tiles amongst themselves.

shuffle_battlefield_rewards.description:
Shuffle the type of reward (Item, XP, GP) given by battlefields and color code them by reward type.
Blue: Give an item. Grey: Give XP. Green: Give GP.

map_shuffle_seed.description:
If this is a number, it will be used as a set seed number for Map, Crest, Battlefield Reward, and Companion shuffles.
If this is "random" the seed will be chosen randomly. If it is any other text, it will be used as a seed group name.
All players using the same seed group name will get the same shuffle results, as long as their Map Shuffle,
Crest Shuffle, Shuffle Battlefield Rewards, Companion Shuffle, and Kaeli's Mom settings are the same.

battlefields_battles_quantities.description: Adjust the number of battles that need to be fought to get a battlefield's reward.

Heretic.name: Heretic

progression_balancing.description:
A system that can move progression earlier, to try and prevent the player from getting stuck and bored early.

A lower setting means more getting stuck. A higher setting means less getting stuck.

accessibility.description:
Set rules for reachability of your items/locations.

**Full:** ensure everything can be reached and acquired.

**Minimal:** ensure what is needed to reach your goal can be acquired.

local_items.description: Forces these items to be in their native world.

non_local_items.description: Forces these items to be outside their native world.

start_inventory.description: Start with the specified amount of these items. Example: "Bomb: 1"

start_hints.description: Start with these item's locations prefilled into the ``!hint`` command.

start_location_hints.description: Start with these locations and their item prefilled into the ``!hint`` command.

exclude_locations.description: Prevent these locations from having an important item.

priority_locations.description: Prevent these locations from having an unimportant item.

item_links.description: Share part of your item pool with other players.

start_inventory_from_pool.description:
Start with the specified amount of these items and don't place them in the world. Example: "Bomb: 1"

The game decides what the replacement items will be.

goal.description:
Choose the main goal.
complete_all_levels: All levels of the selected episodes
complete_boss_levels: Boss levels (E#M8) of selected episodes

difficulty.description:
Choose the game difficulty. These options match Heretic's skill levels.
wet nurse (Thou needeth a wet-nurse) - Fewer monsters and more items than medium. Damage taken is halved, and ammo pickups carry twice as much ammo. Any Quartz Flasks and Mystic Urns are automatically used when the player nears death.
easy (Yellowbellies-r-us) - Fewer monsters and more items than medium.
medium (Bringest them oneth) - Completely balanced, this is the standard difficulty level.
hard (Thou art a smite-meister) - More monsters and fewer items than medium.
black plague (Black plague possesses thee) - Same as hard, but monsters and their projectiles move much faster. Cheating is also disabled.

random_monsters.description:
Choose how monsters are randomized.
vanilla: No randomization
shuffle: Monsters are shuffled within the level
random_balanced: Monsters are completely randomized, but balanced based on existing ratio in the level. (Small monsters vs medium vs big)
random_chaotic: Monsters are completely randomized, but balanced based on existing ratio in the entire game.

random_pickups.description:
Choose how pickups are randomized.
vanilla: No randomization
shuffle: Pickups are shuffled within the level
random_balanced: Pickups are completely randomized, but balanced based on existing ratio in the level. (Small pickups vs Big)

random_music.description:
Level musics will be randomized.
vanilla: No randomization
shuffle_selected: Selected episodes' levels will be shuffled
shuffle_game: All the music will be shuffled

allow_death_logic.description:
Some locations require a timed puzzle that can only be tried once.
After which, if the player failed to get it, the location cannot be checked anymore.
By default, no progression items are placed here. There is a way, hovewer, to still get them:
Get killed in the current map. The map will reset, you can now attempt the puzzle again.

pro.description:
Include difficult tricks into rules. Mostly employed by speed runners.
i.e.: Leaps across to a locked area, trigger a switch behind a window at the right angle, etc.

check_sanity.description:
Include redundant checks. This increase total check count for the game.
i.e.: In a room, there might be 3 checks close to each other. By default, two of them will be remove.
This was done to lower the total count check for Heretic, as it is quite high compared to other games.
Check Sanity restores original checks.

start_with_map_scrolls.description: Give the player all Map Scroll items from the start.

reset_level_on_death.description:
When dying, levels are reset and monsters respawned. But inventory and checks are kept.
Turning this setting off is considered easy mode. Good for new players that don't know the levels well.

death_link.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

episode1.description:
City of the Damned.
If none of the episodes are chosen, Episode 1 will be chosen by default.

episode2.description:
Hell's Maw.
If none of the episodes are chosen, Episode 1 will be chosen by default.

episode3.description:
The Dome of D'Sparil.
If none of the episodes are chosen, Episode 1 will be chosen by default.

episode4.description:

If none of the episodes are chosen, Episode 1 will be chosen by default.

episode5.description:
The Stagnant Demesne.
If none of the episodes are chosen, Episode 1 will be chosen by default.

split_bag_of_holding.description: Split the Bag of Holding into six individual items, each one increasing ammo capacity for one type of weapon only.

bag_of_holding_count.description:
How many Bags of Holding will be available.
If Split Bag of Holding is set, this will be the number of each capacity upgrade available.

max_ammo_crystals.description: Set the starting ammo capacity for crystals (Elven Wand ammo).

max_ammo_arrows.description: Set the starting ammo capacity for arrows (Ethereal Crossbow ammo).

max_ammo_claw_orbs.description: Set the starting ammo capacity for claw orbs (Dragon Claw ammo).

max_ammo_runes.description: Set the starting ammo capacity for runes (Hellstaff ammo).

max_ammo_flame_orbs.description: Set the starting ammo capacity for flame orbs (Phoenix Rod ammo).

max_ammo_spheres.description: Set the starting ammo capacity for spheres (Firemace ammo).

added_ammo_crystals.description: Set the amount of crystal capacity gained when collecting a bag of holding or a capacity upgrade.

added_ammo_arrows.description: Set the amount of arrow capacity gained when collecting a bag of holding or a capacity upgrade.

added_ammo_claw_orbs.description: Set the amount of claw orb capacity gained when collecting a bag of holding or a capacity upgrade.

added_ammo_runes.description: Set the amount of rune capacity gained when collecting a bag of holding or a capacity upgrade.

added_ammo_flame_orbs.description: Set the amount of flame orb capacity gained when collecting a bag of holding or a capacity upgrade.

added_ammo_spheres.description: Set the amount of sphere capacity gained when collecting a bag of holding or a capacity upgrade.

progression_balancing.description:
A system that can move progression earlier, to try and prevent the player from getting stuck and bored early.

A lower setting means more getting stuck. A higher setting means less getting stuck.

accessibility.description:
Set rules for reachability of your items/locations.

**Full:** ensure everything can be reached and acquired.

**Minimal:** ensure what is needed to reach your goal can be acquired.

local_items.description: Forces these items to be in their native world.

non_local_items.description: Forces these items to be outside their native world.

start_inventory.description: Start with the specified amount of these items. Example: "Bomb: 1"

start_hints.description: Start with these item's locations prefilled into the ``!hint`` command.

start_location_hints.description: Start with these locations and their item prefilled into the ``!hint`` command.

exclude_locations.description: Prevent these locations from having an important item.

priority_locations.description: Prevent these locations from having an unimportant item.

item_links.description: Share part of your item pool with other players.

RandomizeDreamers.description:
Allow for Dreamers to be randomized into the item pool and opens their locations for randomization.
This option adds approximately 4 locations.

RandomizeSkills.description:
Allow for Skills, such as Mantis Claw or Shade Soul, to be randomized into the item pool. Also opens their locations
for receiving randomized items.
This option adds approximately 18 locations.

RandomizeFocus.description:
Removes the ability to focus and randomizes it into the item pool.
This option adds approximately 1 location.

RandomizeSwim.description:
Removes the ability to swim in water and randomizes it into the item pool.
This option adds approximately 0 locations.

RandomizeCharms.description:
Allow for Charms to be randomized into the item pool and open their locations for randomization. Includes Charms
sold in shops.
This option adds approximately 45 locations.

RandomizeKeys.description:
Allow for Keys to be randomized into the item pool. Includes those sold in shops.
This option adds approximately 13 locations.

RandomizeMaskShards.description:
Allow for Mask Shard to be randomized into the item pool and open their locations for randomization.
This option adds approximately 16 locations.

RandomizeVesselFragments.description:
Allow for Vessel Fragments to be randomized into the item pool and open their locations for randomization.
This option adds approximately 9 locations.

RandomizeCharmNotches.description:
Allow for Charm Notches to be randomized into the item pool. Includes those sold by Salubra.
This option adds approximately 9 locations.

RandomizePaleOre.description:
Randomize Pale Ores into the item pool and open their locations for randomization.
This option adds approximately 6 locations.

RandomizeGeoChests.description:
Allow for Geo Chests to contain randomized items, as well as their Geo reward being randomized into the item pool.
This option adds approximately 8 locations.

RandomizeJunkPitChests.description:
Randomize the contents of junk pit chests into the item pool and open their locations for randomization.
This option adds approximately 5 locations.

RandomizeRancidEggs.description:
Randomize Rancid Eggs into the item pool and open their locations for randomization
This option adds approximately 20 locations.

RandomizeRelics.description:
Randomize Relics (King's Idol, et al.) into the item pool and open their locations for randomization.
This option adds approximately 43 locations.

RandomizeWhisperingRoots.description:
Randomize the essence rewards from Whispering Roots into the item pool. Whispering Roots will now grant a randomized
item when completed. This can be previewed by standing on the root.
This option adds approximately 15 locations.

RandomizeBossEssence.description:
Randomize boss essence drops, such as those for defeating Warrior Dreams, into the item pool and open their locations
for randomization.
This option adds approximately 12 locations.

RandomizeGrubs.description:
Randomize Grubs into the item pool and open their locations for randomization.
This option adds approximately 46 locations.

RandomizeMimics.description:
Randomize Mimic Grubs into the item pool and open their locations for randomization.
This option adds approximately 4 locations.

RandomizeMaps.description:
Randomize Maps into the item pool. This causes Cornifer to give you a message allowing you to see and buy an item
that is randomized into that location as well.
This option adds approximately 15 locations.

RandomizeStags.description:
Randomize Stag Stations unlocks into the item pool as well as placing randomized items on the stag station bell/toll.
This option adds approximately 11 locations.

RandomizeLifebloodCocoons.description:
Randomize Lifeblood Cocoon grants into the item pool and open their locations for randomization.
This option adds approximately 8 locations.

RandomizeGrimmkinFlames.description:
Randomize Grimmkin Flames into the item pool and open their locations for randomization.
This option adds approximately 10 locations.

RandomizeJournalEntries.description:
Randomize the Hunter's Journal as well as the findable journal entries into the item pool, and open their locations
for randomization. Does not include journal entries gained by killing enemies.
This option adds approximately 6 locations.

RandomizeNail.description:
Removes the ability to swing the nail left, right and up, and shuffles these into the item pool.
This option adds approximately 0 locations.

RandomizeGeoRocks.description:
Randomize Geo Rock rewards into the item pool and open their locations for randomization.
This option adds approximately 207 locations.

RandomizeBossGeo.description:
Randomize boss Geo drops into the item pool and open those locations for randomization.
This option adds approximately 8 locations.

RandomizeSoulTotems.description:
Randomize Soul Refill items into the item pool and open the Soul Totem locations for randomization.
This option adds approximately 59 locations.

RandomizeLoreTablets.description:
Randomize Lore items into the itempool, one per Lore Tablet, and place randomized item grants on the tablets themselves.
You must still read the tablet to get the item.
This option adds approximately 33 locations.

RandomizeElevatorPass.description:
Adds an Elevator Pass item to the item pool, which is then required to use the large elevators connecting
City of Tears to the Forgotten Crossroads and Resting Grounds.

PreciseMovement.description:
Places skips into logic which require extremely precise player movement, possibly without movement skills such as
dash or claw.

ProficientCombat.description: Places skips into logic which require proficient combat, possibly with limited items.

BackgroundObjectPogos.description: Places skips into logic for locations which are reachable via pogoing off of background objects.

EnemyPogos.description: Places skips into logic for locations which are reachable via pogos off of enemies.

ObscureSkips.description: Places skips into logic which are considered obscure enough that a beginner is not expected to know them.

ShadeSkips.description: Places shade skips into logic which utilize the player's shade for pogoing or damage boosting.

InfectionSkips.description: Places skips into logic which are only possible after the crossroads become infected.

FireballSkips.description: Places skips into logic which require the use of spells to reset fall speed while in mid-air.

SpikeTunnels.description: Places skips into logic which require the navigation of narrow tunnels filled with spikes.

AcidSkips.description: Places skips into logic which require crossing a pool of acid without Isma's Tear, or water if swim is disabled.

DamageBoosts.description: Places skips into logic which require you to take damage from an enemy or hazard to progress.

DangerousSkips.description: Places skips into logic which contain a high risk of taking damage.

DarkRooms.description: Places skips into logic which require navigating dark rooms without the use of the Lumafly Lantern.

ComplexSkips.description: Places skips into logic which require intense setup or are obscure even beyond advanced skip standards.

DifficultSkips.description: Places skips into logic which are considered more difficult than typical.

RemoveSpellUpgrades.description: Removes the second level of all spells from the item pool.

StartLocation.description: Choose your start location. This is currently only locked to King's Pass.

Goal.description: The goal required of you in order to complete your run in Archipelago.

GrubHuntGoal.description:
The amount of grubs required to finish Grub Hunt.
On 'All' any grubs from item links replacements etc. will be counted

WhitePalace.description:
Whether or not to include White Palace or not. Note: Even if excluded, the King Fragment check may still be
required if charms are vanilla.

ExtraPlatforms.description: Places additional platforms to make traveling throughout Hallownest more convenient.

AddUnshuffledLocations.description:
Adds non-randomized locations to the location pool, which allows syncing
of location state with co-op or automatic collection via collect.

Note: This will increase the number of location checks required to purchase
hints to the total maximum.

StartingGeo.description: The amount of starting geo you have.

DeathLink.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

DeathLinkShade.description:
Sets whether to create a shade when you are killed by a DeathLink and how to handle your existing shade, if any.

vanilla: DeathLink deaths function like any other death and overrides your existing shade (including geo), if any.
shadeless: DeathLink deaths do not spawn shades. Your existing shade (including geo), if any, is untouched.
shade: DeathLink deaths spawn a shade if you do not have an existing shade. Otherwise, it acts like shadeless.

* This option has no effect if DeathLink is disabled.
** Self-death shade behavior is not changed; if a self-death normally creates a shade in vanilla, it will override
    your existing shade, if any.

DeathLinkBreaksFragileCharms.description:
Sets if fragile charms break when you are killed by a DeathLink.

* This option has no effect if DeathLink is disabled.
** Self-death fragile charm behavior is not changed; if a self-death normally breaks fragile charms in vanilla, it
    will continue to do so.

MinimumGeoPrice.description: The minimum geo price for items in geo shops.

MaximumGeoPrice.description: The maximum geo price for items in geo shops.

MinimumGrubPrice.description: The minimum grub price in the range of prices that an item should cost from Grubfather.

MaximumGrubPrice.description: The maximum grub price in the range of prices that an item should cost from Grubfather.

MinimumEssencePrice.description: The minimum essence price in the range of prices that an item should cost from Seer.

MaximumEssencePrice.description: The maximum essence price in the range of prices that an item should cost from Seer.

MinimumCharmPrice.description:
The minimum charm price in the range of prices that an item should cost for Salubra's shop item which also
carry a charm cost.

MaximumCharmPrice.description:
The maximum charm price in the range of prices that an item should cost for Salubra's shop item which also
carry a charm cost.

RandomCharmCosts.description:
Total Notch Cost of all Charms together. Vanilla sums to 90.
This value is distributed among all charms in a random fashion.
Special Cases:
Set to -1 or vanilla for vanilla costs.
Set to -2 or shuffle to shuffle around the vanilla costs to different charms.

PlandoCharmCosts.description:
Allows setting a Charm's Notch costs directly, mapping {name: cost}.
This is set after any random Charm Notch costs, if applicable.

MinimumEggPrice.description:
The minimum rancid egg price in the range of prices that an item should cost from Jiji.
Only takes effect if the EggSlotShops option is greater than 0.

MaximumEggPrice.description:
The maximum rancid egg price in the range of prices that an item should cost from Jiji.
Only takes effect if the EggSlotShops option is greater than 0.

EggShopSlots.description: For each slot, add a location to the Egg Shop and a filler item to the item pool.

SlyShopSlots.description: For each extra slot, add a location to the Sly Shop and a filler item to the item pool.

SlyKeyShopSlots.description:
For each extra slot, add a location to the Sly Shop (requiring Shopkeeper's Key) and a filler item to the item
pool.

IseldaShopSlots.description: For each extra slot, add a location to the Iselda Shop and a filler item to the item pool.

SalubraShopSlots.description: For each extra slot, add a location to the Salubra Shop, and a filler item to the item pool.

SalubraCharmShopSlots.description:
For each extra slot, add a location to the Salubra Shop (requiring Charms), and a filler item to the item
pool.

LegEaterShopSlots.description: For each extra slot, add a location to the Leg Eater Shop and a filler item to the item pool.

GrubfatherRewardSlots.description: For each extra slot, add a location to the Grubfather and a filler item to the item pool.

SeerRewardSlots.description: For each extra slot, add a location to the Seer and a filler item to the item pool.

ExtraShopSlots.description:
For each extra slot, add a location to a randomly chosen shop a filler item to the item pool.

The Egg Shop will be excluded from this list unless it has at least one item.

Shops are capped at 16 items each.

SplitCrystalHeart.description: Splits the Crystal Heart into left- and right-only versions of the item.

SplitMothwingCloak.description:
Splits the Mothwing Cloak into left- and right-only versions of the item. Randomly adds a second left or
right Mothwing cloak item which functions as the upgrade to Shade Cloak.

SplitMantisClaw.description: Splits the Mantis Claw into left- and right-only versions of the item.

CostSanity.description:
If enabled, most locations with costs (like stag stations) will have randomly determined costs.
If set to shopsonly, CostSanity will only apply to shops (including Grubfather, Seer and Egg Shop).
If set to notshops, CostSanity will only apply to non-shops (e.g. Stag stations and Cornifer locations)

These costs can be in Geo (except Grubfather, Seer and Eggshop), Grubs, Charms, Essence and/or Rancid Eggs

CostSanityHybridChance.description: The chance that a CostSanity cost will include two components instead of one, e.g. Grubs + Essence

CostSanityEggWeight.description: The likelihood of Costsanity choosing a Egg cost. Chosen as a sum of all weights from other types.

CostSanityGrubWeight.description: The likelihood of Costsanity choosing a Grub cost. Chosen as a sum of all weights from other types.

CostSanityEssenceWeight.description: The likelihood of Costsanity choosing a Essence cost. Chosen as a sum of all weights from other types.

CostSanityCharmWeight.description: The likelihood of Costsanity choosing a Charm cost. Chosen as a sum of all weights from other types.

CostSanityGeoWeight.description: The likelihood of Costsanity choosing a Geo cost. Chosen as a sum of all weights from other types.

gesture_shuffle.description: Choose where gestures will appear in the item pool.

medallion_shuffle.description: Shuffles red medallions into the item pool.

extra_items_in_logic.description: Include some extra items in logic (CHARGE UP, 1x PAPER CUP) to prevent the game from becoming too difficult.

**Full:** ensure everything can be reached and acquired.

non_local_items.description: Forces these items to be outside their native world.

start_hints.description: Start with these item's locations prefilled into the ``!hint`` command.

start_location_hints.description: Start with these locations and their item prefilled into the ``!hint`` command.

priority_locations.description: Prevent these locations from having an unimportant item.

start_inventory_from_pool.description:
Start with the specified amount of these items and don't place them in the world. Example: "Bomb: 1"

The game decides what the replacement items will be.

act1_death_link_behaviour.description:
If DeathLink is enabled, determines what counts as a death in act 1. This affects deaths sent and received.

- Sacrificed: Send a death when sacrificed by Leshy. Receiving a death will extinguish all candles.

- Candle Extinguished: Send a death when a candle is extinguished. Receiving a death will extinguish a candle.

goal.description:
Defines the goal to accomplish in order to complete the randomizer.

- Full Story In Order: Complete each act in order. You can return to previously completed acts.

- Full Story Any Order: Complete each act in any order. All acts are available from the start.

- First Act: Complete Act 1 by finding the New Game button. Great for a smaller scale randomizer.

randomize_codes.description: Randomize codes and passwords in the game (clocks, safes, etc.)

randomize_deck.description:
Randomize cards in your deck into new cards.
Disable: Disable the feature.

- Every Encounter Within Same Type: Randomize cards within the same type every encounter (keep rarity/scrybe type).

- Every Encounter Any Type: Randomize cards into any possible card every encounter.

- Starting Only: Only randomize cards given at the beginning of runs and acts.

randomize_sigils.description:
Randomize sigils printed on the cards into new sigils every encounter.

- Disable: Disable the feature.

- Randomize Addons: Only randomize sigils added from sacrifices or other means.

- Randomize All: Randomize all sigils.

optional_death_card.description:
Add a moment after death in act 1 where you can decide to create a death card or not.

- Disable: Disable the feature.

- Always On: The choice is always offered after losing all candles.

- DeathLink Only: The choice is only offered after receiving a DeathLink event.

skip_tutorial.description: Skips the first few tutorial runs of act 1. Bones are available from the start.

skip_epilogue.description: Completes the goal as soon as the required acts are completed without the need of completing the epilogue.

epitaph_pieces_randomization.description:
Determines how epitaph pieces in act 2 are randomized. This can affect your chances of getting stuck.

- All Pieces: Randomizes all nine pieces as their own item.

- In Groups: Randomizes pieces in groups of three.

- As One Item: Group all nine pieces as a single item.

painting_checks_balancing.description:
Generation options for the second and third painting checks in act 1.

- None: Adds no progression logic to these painting checks. They will all count as sphere 1 (early game checks).

- Balanced: Adds rules to these painting checks. Early game items are less likely to appear into these paintings.

- Force Filler: For when you dislike doing these last two paintings. Their checks will only contain filler items.

Jak and Daxter: The Precursor Legacy.name: Jak and Daxter: The Precursor Legacy

progression_balancing.description:
A system that can move progression earlier, to try and prevent the player from getting stuck and bored early.

A lower setting means more getting stuck. A higher setting means less getting stuck.

accessibility.description:
Set rules for reachability of your items/locations.

**Full:** ensure everything can be reached and acquired.

**Minimal:** ensure what is needed to reach your goal can be acquired.

local_items.description: Forces these items to be in their native world.

non_local_items.description: Forces these items to be outside their native world.

start_inventory.description: Start with the specified amount of these items. Example: "Bomb: 1"

start_hints.description: Start with these item's locations prefilled into the ``!hint`` command.

start_location_hints.description: Start with these locations and their item prefilled into the ``!hint`` command.

exclude_locations.description: Prevent these locations from having an important item.

priority_locations.description: Prevent these locations from having an unimportant item.

item_links.description: Share part of your item pool with other players.

enable_move_randomizer.description:
Include movement options as items in the randomizer. Until you find his other moves, Jak is limited to
running, swimming, single-jumping, and shooting yellow eco through his goggles.

This adds 11 items to the pool.

enable_orbsanity.description:
Include bundles of Precursor Orbs as checks. Every time you collect the chosen number of orbs, you will trigger
another check.

Per Level: bundles are for each level in the game.
Global: bundles carry over level to level.

This adds a number of Items and Locations to the pool inversely proportional to the size of the bundle.
For example, if your bundle size is 20 orbs, you will add 100 items to the pool. If your bundle size is 250 orbs,
you will add 8 items to the pool.

global_orbsanity_bundle_size.description:
The orb bundle size for Global Orbsanity. This only applies if "Enable Orbsanity" is set to "Global."
There are 2000 orbs in the game, so your bundle size must be a factor of 2000.

This value is restricted to safe minimum and maximum values to ensure valid singleplayer games and
non-disruptive multiplayer games, but the host can remove this restriction by turning off enforce_friendly_options
in host.yaml.

level_orbsanity_bundle_size.description:
The orb bundle size for Per Level Orbsanity. This only applies if "Enable Orbsanity" is set to "Per Level."
There are 50, 150, or 200 orbs per level, so your bundle size must be a factor of 50.

This value is restricted to safe minimum and maximum values to ensure valid singleplayer games and
non-disruptive multiplayer games, but the host can remove this restriction by turning off enforce_friendly_options
in host.yaml.

fire_canyon_cell_count.description:
The number of power cells you need to cross Fire Canyon. This value is restricted to a safe maximum value to
ensure valid singleplayer games and non-disruptive multiplayer games, but the host can remove this restriction by
turning off enforce_friendly_options in host.yaml.

mountain_pass_cell_count.description:
The number of power cells you need to reach Klaww and cross Mountain Pass. This value is restricted to a safe
maximum value to ensure valid singleplayer games and non-disruptive multiplayer games, but the host can
remove this restriction by turning off enforce_friendly_options in host.yaml.

lava_tube_cell_count.description:
The number of power cells you need to cross Lava Tube. This value is restricted to a safe maximum value to
ensure valid singleplayer games and non-disruptive multiplayer games, but the host can remove this restriction by
turning off enforce_friendly_options in host.yaml.

enable_ordered_cell_counts.description:
Reorder the Cell Count requirements for vehicle sections to be in ascending order.

For example, if Fire Canyon Cell Count, Mountain Pass Cell Count, and Lava Tube Cell Count are 60, 30, and 40
respectively, they will be reordered to 30, 40, and 60.

require_punch_for_klaww.description:
Force the Punch move to come before Klaww. Disabling this setting may require Jak to fight Klaww
and Gol and Maia by shooting yellow eco through his goggles. This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

citizen_orb_trade_amount.description:
The number of orbs you need to trade to citizens for a power cell (Mayor, Uncle, etc.).

Along with Oracle Orb Trade Amount, this setting cannot exceed the total number of orbs in the game (2000).
The equation to determine the total number of trade orbs is (9 * Citizen Trades) + (6 * Oracle Trades).

This value is restricted to a safe maximum value to ensure valid singleplayer games and non-disruptive
multiplayer games, but the host can remove this restriction by turning off enforce_friendly_options in host.yaml.

oracle_orb_trade_amount.description:
The number of orbs you need to trade to the Oracles for a power cell.

Along with Citizen Orb Trade Amount, this setting cannot exceed the total number of orbs in the game (2000).
The equation to determine the total number of trade orbs is (9 * Citizen Trades) + (6 * Oracle Trades).

This value is restricted to a safe maximum value to ensure valid singleplayer games and non-disruptive
multiplayer games, but the host can remove this restriction by turning off enforce_friendly_options in host.yaml.

filler_power_cells_replaced_with_traps.displayName: Filler Power Cells Replaced With Traps
filler_power_cells_replaced_with_traps.description:
The number of filler power cells that will be replaced with traps. This does not affect the number of progression
power cells.

If this value is greater than the number of filler power cells, then they will all be replaced with traps.

filler_orb_bundles_replaced_with_traps.displayName: Filler Orb Bundles Replaced With Traps
filler_orb_bundles_replaced_with_traps.description:
The number of filler orb bundles that will be replaced with traps. This does not affect the number of progression
orb bundles. This only applies if "Enable Orbsanity" is set to "Per Level" or "Global."

If this value is greater than the number of filler orb bundles, then they will all be replaced with traps.

trap_effect_duration.description: The length of time, in seconds, that a trap effect lasts.

trap_weights.description:
The list of traps and corresponding weights that will be randomly added to the item pool. A trap with weight 10 is
twice as likely to appear as a trap with weight 5. Set a weight to 0 to prevent that trap from appearing altogether.
If all weights are 0, no traps are created, overriding the values of "Filler * Replaced With Traps."

jak_completion_condition.description: Set the goal for completing the game.

start_inventory_from_pool.description:
Start with the specified amount of these items and don't place them in the world. Example: "Bomb: 1"

The game decides what the replacement items will be.
